abstract.text: The attributes for a rule that you create.
A human-readable description of the rule.
Code that returns a Boolean or numeric value that the matchmaking rules algorithm executes to compare or filter match requests.
A name for the rule that’s unique within the scope of its rule set.
The type or category of the rule that determines the return value and properties available in the expression.
A numeric value for the rule when `type` is either `DISTANCE` or `MATCH`.

headers: Rules that enforce constraints on two match requests and return a Boolean value. ![spacer] For example, a rule that requires devices to run the same version of your game, or finds players that share a common language or game settings. ![spacer] If you set the `type` field to `COMPATIBLE`, compare the two match requests in the `requests` array in your expression, as in: ![spacer] `areCompatibleAppVersions(requests[0], requests[1])`
rows: Rules that evaluate the similarity of two match requests and return a numeric value between `0.0` and `1.0`. ![spacer] For example, rules that compare the latency or distance between players and find players with the exact same language and region setting. ![spacer] If you set the `type` field to `DISTANCE`, evaluate the two match requests in the `requests` array in your expression, as in: ![spacer] `geoLatency(requests[0], requests[1])`

Rules that evaluate properties across all compatible requests. ![spacer] For example, rules that prefer match candidates with more players but allows less players after a period of time, compare the difference in skill levels of players to a desired skill level that’s a function of time, and find players that have compatible game configurations that loosen over time. ![spacer] If you set the type field to `MATCH`, use the `requests` array in the expression to get all the compatible matches.

Rules that evaluate the assignment of players to teams and return a Boolean value. ![spacer] For example, rules that make the number of players on each team the same, balance the skill levels on each team for a fair match, and keep invited friends on the same team. ![spacer] If you set the `type` field to `TEAM`, use the `teams` array to get all the teams associated with the rule set.

paragraphs.text: The possible values for the `type` field are:

| `COMPATIBLE` | Rules that enforce constraints on two match requests and return a Boolean value. ![spacer] For example, a rule that requires devices to run the same version of your game, or finds players that share a common language or game settings. ![spacer] If you set the `type` field to `COMPATIBLE`, compare the two match requests in the `requests` array in your expression, as in: ![spacer] `areCompatibleAppVersions(requests[0], requests[1])` |
| --- | --- |
| `DISTANCE` | Rules that evaluate the similarity of two match requests and return a numeric value between `0.0` and `1.0`. ![spacer] For example, rules that compare the latency or distance between players and find players with the exact same language and region setting. ![spacer] If you set the `type` field to `DISTANCE`, evaluate the two match requests in the `requests` array in your expression, as in: ![spacer] `geoLatency(requests[0], requests[1])` |
| `MATCH` | Rules that evaluate properties across all compatible requests. ![spacer] For example, rules that prefer match candidates with more players but allows less players after a period of time, compare the difference in skill levels of players to a desired skill level that’s a function of time, and find players that have compatible game configurations that loosen over time. ![spacer] If you set the type field to `MATCH`, use the `requests` array in the expression to get all the compatible matches. |
| `TEAM` | Rules that evaluate the assignment of players to teams and return a Boolean value. ![spacer] For example, rules that make the number of players on each team the same, balance the skill levels on each team for a fair match, and keep invited friends on the same team. ![spacer] If you set the `type` field to `TEAM`, use the `teams` array to get all the teams associated with the rule set. |
